<!-- question-type: inclass -->
### Exercise 7: Requesting multiple years and indicators

So far, we have used `map()` when one input changes and the other stays fixed.

For our final dataset, we want three indicators:

- life expectancy: `"SP.DYN.LE00.IN"`
- population: `"SP.POP.TOTL"`
- GDP per capita: `"NY.GDP.PCAP.CD"`

across every five years from 1960 to 2020.

**(a)** Create a vector called `indicators` containing the three World Bank indicator codes.

```{r}
#| eval: false

indicators <-
  c(
    YOUR_CODE
  )
```

**(b)** Use `expand_grid()` to create every combination of `year` and `indicator`.

```{r}
#| eval: false

requests <-
  expand_grid(
    year = YOUR_CODE,
    indicator = YOUR_CODE
  )
```

Inspect `requests`.

How many rows does it have? What does each row represent?

**(c)** We now want to call `get_indicator()` once for each row of `requests`.
Complete the code below using `map2()`.

```{r}
#| eval: false

indicator_data <-
  map2(
    YOUR_CODE,
    YOUR_CODE,
    YOUR_CODE
  ) |>
  list_rbind()
```

**(d)** Why do we use `map2()` here rather than `map()`?

**(e)** Inspect `indicator_data`.
How does this dataset differ from the `life_expectancy` dataset we created earlier?

<!-- BEGIN PROFILE:r-teaching-guide -->
::: {.content-visible when-profile="r-teaching-guide"}

::: {.teaching-block}

::: {.teaching-block-header}
Teaching Note
:::

::: {.teaching-block-body}

🎯 **Learning Objective**

Students should:

- create a vector of indicator codes;
- use `expand_grid()` to create all combinations of years and indicators;
- use `map2()` when two inputs vary together;
- understand how the rows of `requests` correspond to repeated API calls;
- combine the returned datasets using `list_rbind()`.

✅ **Core Concepts to Highlight**

- `expand_grid()` creates every combination of the values supplied to it.
- Each row of `requests` represents one year–indicator pair.
- `map2()` works through two vectors together.
- Here, the first vector supplies the year and the second supplies the indicator.
- `get_indicator()` is called once for each pair of values.
- We use `map2()` because both inputs vary from one request to the next.
- `list_rbind()` combines the returned datasets into one dataset.

💬 **Suggested In-Class Prompts**

- How many years are in `years`?
- How many indicators are in `indicators`?
- How many rows should `requests` have before we run the code?
- What does the first row of `requests` represent?
- What arguments are passed to `get_indicator()` for that row?
- Why would the `map()` approach from Exercise 5 no longer be enough here?

📌 **Common Misunderstandings**

- Thinking that `expand_grid()` matches values row by row rather than creating all combinations.
- Forgetting that each row of `requests` represents one API request.
- Passing the full `requests` object into `map2()` rather than its two columns.
- Using `map()` even though both year and indicator change across requests.
- Forgetting that the order of the inputs to `map2()` should match the order of the arguments in `get_indicator()`.

:::

:::

:::

<!-- BEGIN PROFILE:r-solutions -->
::: {.content-visible when-profile="r-solutions" when-profile="r-teaching-guide"}

::: {.solution-block}

::: {.solution-block-header}
Solution
:::

::: {.solution-block-body}

(a)

```{r}
indicators <-
  c(
    "SP.DYN.LE00.IN",
    "SP.POP.TOTL",
    "NY.GDP.PCAP.CD"
  )
```

(b)

```{r}
requests <-
  expand_grid(
    year = years,
    indicator = indicators
  )
```

There are 13 years from 1960 to 2020 in steps of five and three indicators, so `requests` has 39 rows.

Each row represents one year–indicator pair that we want to request from the World Bank API.

(c)

```{r}
indicator_data <-
  map2(
    requests$year,
    requests$indicator,
    get_indicator
  ) |>
  list_rbind()
```

(d)

We use `map2()` because two inputs change across requests: the year and the indicator. `map2()` works through these two vectors together and passes each pair of values to `get_indicator()`.

(e)

`life_expectancy` contains one indicator across many years. `indicator_data` contains all three indicators across the same set of years.

:::

:::
